name: More's Utopia: communism, equality, and rational social planning
plain_explanation: Utopia depicts an island society, reported by the fictional traveler Raphael Hythloday, in which all property is held in common, all citizens work only six hours a day, all live in identical houses and dress alike, and religious toleration and mild criminal law prevail -- but Russell notes that such rigid uniformity, however just, would likely be intolerably dull, since diversity seems essential to happiness.
precise_definition: Russell's description of Utopia as a Republic-like communist society in which 'the public good cannot flourish where there is private property, and without communism there can be no equality,' organized around identical towns, communal dining, universal (short) working hours, elected officials drawn from a learned class, and tolerant but compulsory theism, while noting Russell's own reservation: 'life in More's Utopia, as in most others, would be intolerably dull. Diversity is essential to happiness... This is a defect of all planned social systems, actual as well as imaginary.'
why_it_mattered: Represents an early modern articulation of a communist, egalitarian social ideal directly indebted to Plato's Republic, notable for genuinely liberal elements (opposition to the death penalty for theft, religious toleration, opposition to war for glory, kindness to animals) mixed with features modern readers would find illiberal (compulsory dress and housing rotation, harsh punishment of premarital sex).
historical_origin: Published in 1518, modeled explicitly on Plato's Republic.
examples: Six-hour workdays, with surplus labor rewarded by even shorter hours
Contempt for gold, used only for chamberpots and bondmen's chains
Opposition to the death penalty for theft, opening the book's argument
A eloquent passage against hunting and the wanton killing of animals
objections: Russell's own objection: uniformity and lack of private property would make life 'intolerably dull,' since diversity is essential to happiness -- 'a defect of all planned social systems'
The character 'More' in the dialogue itself objects that communism would make men idle and destroy respect for magistrates
competing_positions: Plato's Republic, on which Utopia is explicitly modeled
influence_on_later_thinkers: Named the entire literary and political genre of 'utopian' thought.
connection_to_politics_or_religion: Utopians are converted to Christianity partly because they learn Christ opposed private property; multiple religions are tolerated, but atheists are excluded from citizenship.
